invariant: Java's command candidate owns a complete multiline note as one syntactic unit before later commands are considered. Command regexes are case-insensitive. Floating entity notes use note-as plus end-note; attached entity notes additionally admit a final-bracket form; sequence note, hnote, and rnote openers retain their shape and may close with the note-family END regex. Interior lines are display payload, never sibling commands, while commands after the legal terminator remain visible.
causal_divergence: Rust has four partial note grammars. Dispatch hides only ordinary note blocks ending in the spaced end-note form. The class parser matches lowercase ordinary openers and has no final-bracket buffer state. The deployment parser has a buffer only for attached notes, so a Java-valid floating note-as block is ignored and its body becomes DESCRIPTION entities. The sequence parser recognizes hnote/rnote openers but closes its buffer only for ordinary end-note, so those complete commands disappear. These are manifestations of a missing command-boundary model, not independent keyword-score constants.
planned_change: Introduce shared parser-level note keyword and terminator classification, then make dispatch and the class, deployment, and sequence consumers use it. Completed-span discovery will recognize ordinary, hnote, and rnote families, case-insensitive end-note variants, and the attached final-bracket form without hiding unterminated source. Class parsing will retain the chosen terminator while buffering and match opener grammar case-insensitively. Deployment will create and buffer floating note-as commands instead of exposing their payload as nodes. Sequence will retain the opener's shape and accept Java's complete note-family terminator set. No output coordinates or comparator behavior change in this mechanism.
perturbation_axes: ordinary note versus hnote versus rnote
floating note-as versus attached note versus message note
end-note terminator versus final closing bracket
post-terminator class, deployment, and sequence commands
renamed targets, aliases, colors, and changed body line counts
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns command boundary recognition and construction of the corresponding parser note model. It does not own class SVEK placement of multiple already-parsed floating notes, note paint geometry, link routing, comparator tolerance, baselines, or fixture eligibility.
acceptance: The preserved note-only dispatch cases and the fresh bracketed, mixed-case, DESCRIPTION, hnote, and rnote counterexamples parse to the Java-selected subtype and retain every note body as note payload
Parser tests exercise at least two independent grammar axes per affected consumer and prove post-terminator commands remain visible
Unterminated inputs do not hide arbitrary trailing source
All parser unit tests and relevant diff_one --no-oracle perturbations pass except separately-accounted renderer divergences
An independent checker generates fresh valid held-outs and records an accepted verdict at the implementation revision
forbidden_approaches: special-casing payload words, fixture aliases, or checker filenames
forcing every note-leading source to one subtype
treating all closing braces as note terminators
changing comparator tolerance, baselines, or fixture eligibility
